decisions.reason: The digital anamnesis and consent app sits close to the core practice software, costs little to maintain, and gained strategic value as practices digitalized after 2020, so the option is worth keeping open.
The continuing education institute builds on the firm's existing training resources, strengthens customer ties at low incremental cost, and has no evidence of failure, so it stays.
Remote screen sharing support is a cheap, integral part of customer support whose value rose with remote work, so dropping it would not free meaningful resources.
The analytics dashboard extends the core data offer toward connected, efficiently managed practices, its prospects are still uncertain but promising, and holding it costs little.
The complete practice bundle mainly repackages existing modules for new and larger practices, so it costs little to keep and supports sales of the core offer.

The listing portal is distant from the core business and only mentioned on the website, which makes it the weakest option, but it is cheap to run and its value is still unresolved, so it is kept for now while being watched closely.
